title: What's New in 0.1.57
items: If ElevenLabs or xAI rejects your account or key, for example after a failed payment, Murmur now says so in the recording window, the menu bar and Settings, with a link to fix it.
While a provider is refusing, dictation goes straight to the on-device engine instead of waiting on cloud attempts that will fail, and tries the cloud again every 5 minutes.
Settings has a Check now button to test the provider again as soon as you've fixed it.

title: What's New in 0.1.56
items: Edit text by voice: select text in any app, hold the dictation key, and say what to change, or dictate new text to replace it.
Long dictations are no longer cut at a brief quiet moment, so words between sentences are kept.
Words you keep correcting are now suggested for your dictionary, and nothing changes until you click Add.
Apple's built-in speech recognition is available as an on-device engine, and is the default for new installs without a key or downloaded model.
Choose your microphone in Settings, mark microphones to never use, and get a hint when the mic gives no audio or the level is very low.
Text goes to the app you were in when you released the key, and ordinary dictations are no longer stopped by a false change-of-field warning.
Fixed Transcribing staying on screen after a short silent hold, and speech is kept in History if the microphone fails mid-hold.
Optional Apple voice isolation for the microphone, off by default.
The Dictionary shows the correct spelling first with what Murmur heard beneath it, in A to Z order.
Numbers are written as digits and your dictionary words are used on the ElevenLabs fallback path.
Murmur's temporary clipboard use no longer syncs to your other devices.
A new waveform menu-bar icon, plus accessibility, contrast and Reduce Motion improvements throughout.

title: What's New in 0.1.55
items: Settings is now split into sections, and Permissions shows which grants are in place with a button to fix any that are missing.
The menu-bar icon can pause dictation and check for updates.
Transforms set to on-device no longer fall back to a cloud service when the on-device model is unavailable.
A long recording is no longer lost when saved audio is over its storage limit.
Cleanup can no longer drop a sentence, a "not", or a number from what you said.
Fixed a case where text could be pasted twice, and one where a similar sentence was removed as a duplicate.
Insights shows formatted totals and a clearer activity heatmap.

title: What's New in 0.1.54
items: A dictation no longer disappears and highlights everything in the text field, which let the next dictation replace your text.
Holding Command, Option, or Control while a dictation is being typed no longer turns it into a keyboard shortcut.

title: What's New in 0.1.53
items: An accidental tap of the dictation key is ignored instead of leaving Transcribing on screen.
The Transcribing panel can no longer stay up indefinitely; a late result is saved to History instead of being typed into another app.
ElevenLabs dictation avoids an unnecessary second transcription when the final text has already arrived.
Releasing the key before a live connection is ready recovers from the recording right away.
Emoji are typed intact, and a paste that already landed is never repeated.
Filler removal leaves the word um alone in languages other than English.
Saying forward slash now joins short words such as PP/shipped when code-aware mode is on.
Removing an API key asks for confirmation, and deleting a History entry also deletes its recording.
Saved data is protected from being overwritten when a file cannot be read at launch.
Murmur quits cleanly when asked to, even with a sheet open.

title: What's New in 0.1.52
items: Text that the system delivers late is no longer typed a second time.
Your clipboard is restored correctly when two dictations happen back to back.
Switching microphones mid-dictation no longer garbles the recording or discards it when you release during the switch.
Voice enrollment no longer crashes when the default microphone is unavailable.
Spoken capitalization commands no longer remove words or punctuation from ordinary sentences.
Editing a failed History entry or a pronoun no longer teaches the dictionary bad replacements.
xAI dictation keeps short phrases you intentionally repeat.
Gemini and Muse fall back quickly when their connection stalls instead of hanging.

title: What's New in 0.1.51
items: xAI dictation now uses Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0, xAI's newest and most accurate speech-to-text model, for both live streaming and recorded audio.

title: What's New in 0.1.50
items: Dictation in Safari now uses a single paste to prevent reordered text in web editors.
Optional filler cleanup removes standalone um and uh conservatively, preserving quoted text and code.
Stalled cloud streams and local transcription processes now exit through bounded recovery paths.
Retrying a recording saves the result in History without inserting it into the current app.
Voice-profile saves and recording exports preserve the previous file if replacement fails.
ElevenLabs advanced settings now explain that background-voice filtering can also omit quieter speech.
AssemblyAI dictation uses the current supported transcription models.

title: What's New in 0.1.49
items: Improved preservation of final words during audio capture, cloud conversion, and recovery from incomplete live transcripts.
Recognized sound labels such as coughing and sniffling are removed from dictation while ordinary parenthetical text is preserved.
Missing final periods are added to ordinary prose, with safeguards for code, formatting, and edits within existing text.
ElevenLabs skips a redundant streaming wait when complete-recording recovery is already required.
Successful streaming recordings can be retried from History within the existing audio-retention limit.

title: What's New in 0.1.48
items: Long dictations keep their ending: cloud streaming now recovers words the live transcript dropped at release, with extra mic grace on holds over 15 seconds.
Meta Muse Voice Transcribe is a new cloud engine in Settings — add a Meta API key for live streaming or batch fallback.
Opening sentences are captured reliably again: the mic starts when you press the key while the stream connects in the background.

title: What's New in 0.1.47
items: Dictation accuracy: the phonetic auto-correction that maps mishears to your dictionary terms no longer rewrites real English words — only genuine mishears get corrected.
Your last word survives: the mic now captures a brief grace period after you release the dictation key, so trailing words aren't clipped mid-syllable.

title: What's New in 0.1.46
items: Stamped out the last duplicate-dictation path: delivery retries now require hard evidence that text didn't arrive before trying again, instead of trusting a confirmation channel that can go blind under system load.
A dictation that can't be verified is accepted once and kept in History — never delivered twice.

title: What's New in 0.1.45
items: Fixed doubled dictation: a brief system stall could make Murmur type the same transcript twice. Delivery retries now wait out slow event delivery instead of re-typing.
Long dictations that hit the 10-minute Gemini session cap keep everything transcribed so far instead of coming back empty.

title: What's New in 0.1.44
items: Dictation no longer overwrites your clipboard on the normal path — text is typed in, and paste is only a fallback.
Very short accidental holds at the silence floor no longer flash a false “Transcription failed.”
Cloud Advanced captions spell out what each control does; Acknowledgements sit behind an Open-source licenses disclosure.
What's New in Settings shows the latest release first, with earlier ones one tap away.
Apple Silicon only from here on (Intel builds dropped). Sparkle, WhisperKit, and FluidAudio are updated underneath.

title: What's New in 0.1.43
items: The dictionary keeps every misspelling of a word on that one word, instead of splitting it across duplicate rows.
Recent corrections can be hidden without undoing a mapping you still want. Revert still removes a bad misspelling without deleting the rest of the word.

title: What's New in 0.1.42
items: Google Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Live is now a Settings cloud engine for everyone — add a Gemini API key and pick it the same way as Grok or ElevenLabs.
If the live Gemini connection fails, Murmur falls back to Gemini batch transcription.

title: What's New in 0.1.41
items: Dictation can no longer learn a correction that rewrites an everyday word like “type” into another word. A one-off transcription glitch now stays one-off instead of becoming a permanent rule.

title: What's New in 0.1.40
items: Holding to talk no longer drops the start of a sentence when Continuity Camera appears. The listening sound waits until the microphone is actually live.
iPhone and virtual mics stay off unless you turn on fallback in Settings.
Everyday phrases like “line out” are no longer rewritten to jargon from your dictionary.

title: What's New in 0.1.39
items: When the Mac microphone is the Sound Input default, Murmur binds it even if Core Audio has already offered another live device.

title: What's New in 0.1.38
items: Murmur still tries your Mac microphone when Core Audio briefly reports it as format-dead or not alive, instead of jumping to Continuity Camera or Jump Desktop.

title: What's New in 0.1.37
items: Holding the dictation key no longer force-quits Murmur.
Murmur uses your Mac microphone instead of Continuity Camera or Jump Desktop unless that is what Sound Input is set to.
If the first microphone bind fails, it retries a working device instead of showing Microphone unavailable.

title: What's New in 0.1.36
items: If a headset or other microphone unplugs while Murmur is running, it now switches to a working mic instead of freezing until you force-quit.
A stuck microphone start times out instead of locking the dictation key.

title: What's New in 0.1.35
items: Saying “exclamation point” or “question mark” at the end of a sentence now inserts ! or ? instead of writing the words.
Talking about a mark — “a question mark”, “an exclamation point” — still stays words.

title: What's New in 0.1.34
items: Dictionary terms and snippet triggers that begin or end with punctuation — “.net”, “@work”, “c++” — now actually apply. They could always be saved, but they never matched anything you said.
Corrections no longer double up punctuation: dictating “we ship on .net” could come back as “we ship on ..NET”.

title: What's New in 0.1.33
items: Editing a dictionary term, snippet, or transform can no longer blank out the field that does the work — a change that would have quietly deleted words from later dictations is now refused.
Per-app Style assignment now applies to the app you were last working in, instead of always assigning to Murmur itself.
Opening a Scratchpad note no longer marks it as edited just for looking at it.
The confirmation pill stays up long enough to read: dictionary fix counts and the “left on clipboard” warning no longer vanish in half a second, and the live preview shows a third line of text.

title: What's New in 0.1.32
items: An accidental split-second tap of the dictation key is now quietly ignored instead of ending in a “Transcription failed” error after a long wait.
Real quiet speech is unaffected — soft-spoken holds still get the full transcription treatment.

title: What's New in 0.1.31
items: Dictation now types into whatever app you are in when you release the key. Start a thought in one window, walk to another, and the text lands where you finish — no more transcripts left on the clipboard because you moved.
If another app steals focus while Murmur is still transcribing, the text is still left on the clipboard rather than pasted into the wrong window.

title: What's New in 0.1.30
items: Dictation recovers automatically when another app's voice feature leaves the microphone silently dead — no more empty holds after switching back to Murmur.
If the microphone is rerouted mid-dictation, capture restarts in place and keeps what you already said instead of losing the rest of the hold.
The on-device fallback can no longer hang forever loading its model — a stuck load now fails visibly and keeps the recording so you can retry from History.

title: What's New in 0.1.29
items: Dictation no longer wipes images, files, or formatted text you had copied — the full clipboard is restored afterward.
The "copied to clipboard" flash only appears when the text really is on the clipboard, and failed injections now leave it there to paste yourself.
Cloud transcription, cleanup, and transforms time out instead of hanging indefinitely when the network stalls.
The recording storage limit in Settings is now the actual limit — retention was previously capped at 5 recordings regardless of the size you picked.
Transforms run on the cleanup backend you selected, including xAI Grok, instead of always using OpenAI.
The transform hotkey reports success or failure in the HUD, and the menu shows the correct version.

title: What's New in 0.1.28
items: Streaming holds that showed interim words no longer vanish without injecting or logging history.
Empty streaming commits keep the last partial transcript instead of wiping it.
Discarded silence or empty holds now appear as failed rows in History so ghosts are visible.

title: What's New in 0.1.27
items: Continuation dictation gets a leading space again when Accessibility cannot read the caret.
Switching apps mid-hold leaves the transcript on the clipboard with an error instead of pasting into the wrong app.
Rapid same-text re-dictation no longer flashes a fake success or adds a duplicate history row.

title: What's New in 0.1.26
items: Mid-sentence select-replace strips ASR trailing punctuation and false Title Case when Accessibility can read the field.
Code-aware mode is its own Settings toggle — no longer hidden under Cleanup.
When Accessibility cannot read the caret, Murmur no longer prepends an extra leading space.

title: What's New in 0.1.25
items: Replacing selected mid-sentence words no longer leaves a stray period from short ASR clips when Smart leading space is on.

title: What's New in 0.1.24
items: Spoken capitalization commands still work when dictation glues a period onto the letter (e.g. capital S.).

title: What's New in 0.1.23
items: Dictionary Recent corrections and Auto-learned scroll with the list, including when the dictionary is empty.
Revert, Never, and Restore dismiss the acted-on correction from Recent corrections.
Say capital X (or NATO letters like capital kilo) to capitalize that letter in dictation.

title: What's New in 0.1.22
items: When Murmur learns a correction, a system toast appears with Reject to undo and stop learning that pair.
Accepted and rejected learns show in Dictionary → Corrections, with Restore and Revert / Never actions.

title: What's New in 0.1.21
items: Learn from corrections in other apps: when you fix a misspelled word after dictation, Murmur can add it to your dictionary automatically (Settings → Dictionary).
Toggle is on by default; turn it off anytime to stop watching for inline edits.

title: What's New in 0.1.20
items: Sparkle update dialog now shows release notes from the same bundled What's New catalog.
What's New is still available anytime in Settings → What's New.

title: What's New in 0.1.19
items: What's New: after an update you'll see a short summary once, and you can re-read it anytime in Settings → What's New.
WhisperKit model files now live under Application Support instead of Documents, with a one-time migration from the old location.
Model cache migration and usable-cache checks are hardened so a partial or stale download is less likely to block dictation.
Public-repo scrub: operator paths and credential-store references removed from shipped plan docs ahead of open-source release.

title: What's New in 0.1.18
items: WhisperKit model cache path and migration hardening (Application Support).
Repository prep for an upcoming public release (LICENSE, contributing guidelines, and related housekeeping).
In-app updates via Sparkle continue from the same feed.
